title: 'I thought it was a UFO': Middle Tennessee gets early glimpse of SpaceX rocket launch
excerpt: Residents across Middle Tennessee recall waking up to a rare sight in the sky Tuesday morning, as SpaceX launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
content:
Nikki McGee

Updated Tue, October 13, 2026 at 11:07 PM UTC

NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WKRN) -- Residents across Middle Tennessee recall waking up to a rare sight in the sky Tuesday morning, as SpaceX launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida.

“I thought it was a UFO or something, and I don't necessarily believe in that. I know I sound crazy, but I thought it was going to be a UFO or something worse, so I'm glad it's not,” said Rob Bennett, who lives in Hendersonville. “I was just still trying to wake up with no caffeine and piece this all together.” 

SEE ALSO | SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launch spotted over TN

Bennett captured video of the launch while out on his 5 a.m. walk before sunrise.  

“I did notice it had this weird tail to it and kind of a bulb-shaped. So I started filming it so someone would believe me or I could verify it later,” he said.  

The rocket, which some described as looking like a jelly fish, is headed to the International Space Station with several types of biomaterial, which will be used in several medical experiments.

Several of those especially stand out to Janet Ivey, President and CEO of Janet’s Planet. 

“For these particular missions, they figure out how to 3D print a heart that could have, you know, all kinds of benefits for people in space and on earth or to create perfect retinal implants, and you do that in microgravity rather than the imperfection that happens here on Earth,” she explained. “Then, if you solve or figure out biomarkers early enough that you could target Alzheimer's and Parkinson's—think about how revolutionary that can be.”

The space craft is set to return to earth in mid-November.  

“As it launched, it kind of created this glowing space jellyfish. Basically, it was kind of this atmospheric effect visible for several states. So, just seeing that is the reminder to all of us that we're already a human space-faring species. We're attempting to do great science off-world to benefit us here on Earth,” Ivey added.
